convention: This file carries POINTERS AND TRAPS, not retellings. A задача is cited by its section in PLAN.md or SPEC.md, never paraphrased here: a paraphrase is a second copy of the truth and it drifts (it already did once, for routing_lists). What belongs here instead: file and symbol pointers, measured facts, rejected shapes with their arguments, and the traps that cost the last passes time. Written down in full in implementation-notes.md, section 'doclint — утверждение документа о состоянии обязано опираться на исполнимое'.

measurement_vs_inference.rule: A measurement and the conclusion drawn from it are TWO statements, and this file must keep them apart. Record what was run and what it printed; record separately what you concluded, and name the steps between. A conclusion written as if it were the measurement is inherited by the next pass as measured fact.
measurement_vs_inference.why_this_block_exists: The previous HANDOFF said, citing a live run, that the agent holds the store's exclusive flock for its whole life and therefore `hop nodes` refuses while the tunnel is up. The run was real and still reproduces: `flock -x <root>/.lock sleep 8 &` then `hop nodes` → exit 1 after 5043 ms. The conclusion was wrong, and two inference steps did the damage: (1) 'the agent holds the store' → 'the agent holds the lock' — `store.Open` takes no lock, `load()` reads all three files without one, and the lock lives inside `transact`, per transaction (measured: 559 transactions, mean 1.05 ms); (2) 'the lock is held' → 'a reader waits' — a reader takes no lock at all. Both steps were invisible because the sentence read like a measurement.

closed_this_pass.the_measurement_that_shaped_the_guard: `systemd-analyze verify` RETURNS ZERO on a broken unit. systemd 261, one directive broken at a time: Restart=когда-нибудь → rc 0 + «Failed to parse»; Type=exek → rc 0 + «Failed to parse»; Frobnicate=1 → rc 0 + «Unknown key»; WantedBy=нет-такой.target → rc 0 and NO OUTPUT AT ALL; missing ExecStart → rc 1; [Servise] → rc 1. So the guard reds on ANY OUTPUT, not on the exit code — a code-only test would have passed three breaks of six — and the [Install] target is checked by a separate assertion because verify does not check it at all.
closed_this_pass.two_verify_quirks_worth_inheriting: `--root=DIR` needs the WHOLE unit tree inside that root («Unit sysinit.target not found»), so the guard builds its root from the machine's /usr/lib/systemd/system with the staging on top. And `--user` together with `--root` does not work at all («Failed to initialize unit search paths for root directory … Invalid argument»), so the user unit is verified under system-manager rules: syntax and directive values yes, user-session semantics no. Named in the test's own comment.
closed_this_pass.shape_decisions_not_to_reopen: (1) The units pass NO flags: -socket and -group are already the product's defaults, and copying them into a unit makes a second source of truth that drifts silently (the unit is edited under root, the default in code). The seam is held by a test that compares install.sh's GROUP= with the AST default of hopd's -group. (2) No -prefix in the script for the same reason: a prefix means rewriting ExecStart on the fly, i.e. a third copy of the path. (3) No sandboxing directives at all: hopd opens /dev/net/tun and shells out to `ip`, every Protect*/Private* can turn fail-close into fail-broken, and nothing here can measure the consequence. Hardening arrives with the CI job that can observe it.
closed_this_pass.readiness_is_not_expressible_and_the_uni: Type=exec is the honest maximum: no sd_notify, no socket activation. systemd calls hopd started after a successful exec, i.e. BEFORE /run/hop.sock is listening. For the user unit it does not matter at all — systemd --user is a separate hierarchy and After= on a system unit does not work from it — so the race «login overtook hopd» cannot be closed in unit files. RestartSec=2s buys it a ten-second window (machine defaults DefaultStartLimitBurst=5, DefaultStartLimitIntervalUSec=10s) and then a visible failed unit instead of an endless loop. That arithmetic is DERIVED from two measured defaults, not measured end-to-end; only «`hop agent` exits 2 immediately with no service» is measured.
closed_this_pass.controls: All seven guards reddened by hand, each with its own message: verb `agentt` in ExecStart; flag -socket there; GROUP=hopd; ExecStart pointing outside the staging; the user unit moved into the system directory; Restart=когда-нибудь (the rc-0 one); WantedBy=нет-такой.target; systemctl called in staging mode; uninstall forgetting the user unit; the existence check merged with the write («отказ случился после записи: в раскладке уже лежит /usr/bin/hop»); and — found in acceptance, not by a test — the real-mode root check standing AFTER the first write, so `install.sh install` without sudo died on `install -D` with the kernel's «Permission denied» instead of the product's refusal. Fixed in a9d4ea6; the eighth guard, TestRealInstallRefusesWithoutRootBeforeTouchingAnything, skips when the gate itself runs as root — a real install on the machine running `go test` is forbidden by the §6.13 decision and must never happen silently.

gate.rule_learned: The L3 line is part of the gate, not an optional extra — a pass that changed only the CLI surface (ef9027d) once left the whole internal/l3 package red and the other five commands did not see it. Any pass touching cmd/hop, internal/ipc or internal/agent must run it, and the controller must re-run it on the MERGED tree.

notes.doclint: Fast. CI runs it as `go run ./cmd/doclint -git=false .` — a checkout has neither the pass branches nor the full history, so the git half is off there and on locally.
notes.negcheck: runs every guard twice (with/without its policy) via `go test -count=1`; 48 policies as of this pass, ~25-35 min wall clock — expected, not a hang; don't rely on go test's cache. It needs permission to listen on loopback: a network-restricted sandbox creates false oracle defects. There is no per-policy selection: for a per-task gate run the new policy's own guard under HOP_DISABLE=<name> by hand; the controller runs the full one at the end. TWO TRAPS MEASURED THIS ROUND, both from running it in the background while working. (1) It races your edits: negcheck re-runs `go test` for ~30 minutes, so a tree edited mid-run gets compiled half-edited and the report is a wall of «ДЕФЕКТ ОРАКУЛА … undefined: slices» that says nothing about any policy. Start it only on a tree you have stopped touching. (2) It is load, and load is what the gate's flakes need: `go test ./...` beside a running negcheck is what exposed the W66 flake this round — useful on purpose, ruinous by accident, because a red then has two possible authors.
notes.realtimelint: does not accept ./... as an argument — pass literally `.`
notes.l3_how_to_run: `go test -c -o /tmp/l3.test ./internal/l3` then `HOP_L3=1 unshare -Urn /tmp/l3.test` (add `-test.v -test.run '<pattern>'` to scope it). No root needed — unshare -Urn grants CAP_NET_ADMIN in a fresh netns. Reuse the built binary across runs. WITHOUT -test.v the package prints only a final PASS, and a fully-skipped package prints the same PASS: count `--- PASS` lines (19 as of this pass, zero SKIP) before believing it ran. Name what unshare does NOT isolate: $HOME (hence per-test HOP_STORE) and $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (hence per-test -client-socket).
notes.known_red_that_is_not_yours: go vet ./... is red at internal/engine/dialer.go (copylocks in xray-core's SocketConfig). realtimelint is red with 3 hits in internal/dnstest/realserver_test.go. gofmt -l ./internal reports internal/l2/dns_test.go. All three predate these passes; the honest gate is 'no NEW findings', compared on the full output rather than the exit code. Capture the baseline before starting — it makes acceptance a diff instead of a judgement.
notes.flake: Three found and fixed across two rounds, and none of them was about clocks. internal/l2 TestT10SlowNodeKeepsConnectionAlive: 0 red in 400 runs under 16 busy loops (was 8 of 200). internal/health TestA22PinnedNodeIsNotReplacedWhenDead: 0 red in 5×10 under -race (was 2 of 3). internal/agent TestW66NodesCarryLiveHealthNotTheDiskSlice, NEW this round: 0 red in 160 runs under load (was 4 of 5 runs × 20) — see closed_this_pass. The pattern all three share: the test waited for an event that is not the one it needed, and the missing wait was invisible on an idle machine. What REMAINS worth knowing: A22's flake and a genuine break of the pinned-node mechanism print the SAME message («состояние B = alive, ожидалось dead»); the L2 stand is load-sensitive by construction; and the load that has now exposed two of the three is simply RUNNING TWO TEST RUNS AT ONCE — negcheck beside `go test ./...` is the cheapest way to reproduce it deliberately.
notes.what_is_not_a_flake: cmd/hop/measure_test.go compares against time in exactly one place — `hop nodes` must return 0 — and the margin there is three orders of magnitude. A refusal in that test is a regression, not load. The 'longest held' numbers it logs are not assertions and move freely on a busy machine.
notes.negative_control_on_l3_can_lie: Found by the orphan-up pass, and it will bite the next one. internal/l3 builds `hop` and `hopd` itself (buildOnce, harness_test.go) and FAILS the test on a build error — UNLESS HOP_L3_BIN_HOP / HOP_L3_BIN_HOPD are set, and then it silently uses the binaries they name. So a hand-made break that does not COMPILE gives a GREEN L3 run against the previous binary, and the green reads as «the guard is vacuous» when it actually means «the break never happened». When reddening an L3 guard by hand: either unset HOP_L3_BIN_*, or rebuild them after every edit, and make the break compile (e.g. tunnel.Phase("такой фазы нет") instead of deleting a comparison and orphaning its import).
notes.fake_clock_hole_left_open: clock.Fake.After(d) with d <= 0 never fires on its own, while the real time.After(0) fires immediately. The flakes pass deliberately did NOT fix it and said why: the fix would make the number of probe-loop turns unpredictable, and T6 and A24 assert on that count. Verified by reading internal/clock/fake.go. Anyone hitting a fake-clock test that hangs should look here first.

autostart_decision.what_was_decided: §6.13's second and third thirds (autostart of the SERVICE and of the AGENT). Decided by the human this round, after the facts below were gathered. The decision is recorded here and NOT yet implemented: the pass that takes it implements it, it does not re-open it.
autostart_decision.facts_that_shaped_it: (1) Nothing about packaging exists in the repo: no Makefile, no scripts, no unit/plist/wxs, dist/ is gitignored. (2) hopd has no service-manager integration at all — flags -socket /run/hop.sock, -group hop, -ready-file, foreground, SIGTERM → teardown + snapshot verify; no sd_notify, no socket activation, no SCM. (3) MEASURED this round: `hop agent` does not wait for the service and does not retry — with no hopd it prints «фоновая половина hop недоступна: сокет /run/hop.sock: dial unix …: connect: no such file or directory» and exits 2, immediately. (4) macOS and Windows dataplanes are honest errors from platform.New(), so an installer for them cannot be tested here.
autostart_decision.decision_1_scope: Units + a dev-install script NOW; .deb/.rpm/.pkg/MSI stay queued. PLAN §9 promises the packages in this stage, so this is a deliberate deferral and must be recorded as such: the packages arrive with the platforms that can be tested. PLAN already allows exactly this shape («До этого этапа допустим только локальный dev-install»).
autostart_decision.decision_2_registration: Declarative: unit files (and later a plist) shipped as FILES; nothing in the product knows about systemd. No `hop service install` verb — it would mean editing §5.9 in SPEC.md (cmd/hop reads the verb list FROM the spec) and a second source of truth about the unit. The asymmetry is deliberate and expected: Windows SCM has no declarative form, so registration there arrives as code inside hopd together with the Windows dataplane.
autostart_decision.decision_3_agent_at_login: `systemctl --global enable hop-agent.service` — the package (today: the dev-install script) enables the user unit for every user session. That is what §8.5 I1 requires after a standard install, with no second action from the human.
autostart_decision.decision_4_group: The install creates group `hop` and adds $SUDO_USER to it, printing loudly what it did and that membership carries the right to raise the tunnel (§6.1 authorizes the control socket by group). The person running the installer is by definition the machine's admin, and §5.10 promises a single sudo for the product's whole life. Membership takes effect at the next login — which is when the agent starts anyway.
autostart_decision.what_this_exposes_and_does_NOT_fix: Fact (3) above is a product defect that autostart at login turns into a restart loop: a user not yet in group `hop`, or a login racing hopd, gets an agent that dies at once. The fix belongs to the product (the agent must survive an unreachable service: stay up, answer `hop status` with code 2, attach when the service appears) and is NOT in the autostart pass — it touches cmd/hop and internal/agent, which the orphan-up pass holds this round. It is the queue item `агент не переживает недоступный сервис` below. docs/not-yet-written.md already names internal/supervisor («надзор за сервисом») — if that fix introduces the package, the line must go, the list is red in both directions.
autostart_decision.verification_available_here: `systemd-analyze verify` exists on this machine (systemd 261) and needs no root and no installation. There is NO container runtime (no docker, no podman) — systemd-nspawn exists but has no rootfs. So the honest split is: unit files verified by systemd-analyze; the install script verified against a staging DESTDIR; and the REAL install (`sudo`, enable --now, is-active, then removal) only in a CI job on a disposable runner, which is unverified locally and must say so — the same status the l3-macos.yml and l3-windows.yml skeletons already carry. Nothing is to be installed on the developer's own machine.
autostart_decision.implemented_by: de922ac. The four answers were implemented, not reopened. What the implementation ADDED to them is in closed_this_pass → shape_decisions_not_to_reopen (no flags in units, no -prefix, no sandboxing) and in the systemd-analyze measurement. This block stays because the decision's REASONS are not repeated in the units, only its shape.
